description: Compose declared box behaviour (carrier `values`, box `behavior` rows) into the model's external relation: boundary inputs (unwired input ports) to deliverables (product input ports fed by a non-harmful function). The default upstream scope composes boxes that can reach a deliverable and explicitly assumes omitted boxes accept everything; scope whole composes every box, including downstream and disconnected constraints. full_relation returns all rows within the search cap. Feedback loops compose by the relational trace, so every consistent steady state counts, and the steady states are listed. `factorisations` lists each composed box whose relation is the product of its projections onto two or more groups of ports, with the finest groups, in box order (decided:false past a per-box cap): segment it into them, or unions of them, and each part keeps its projection. The hint describes the declared rows, not a physical split, and changes no verdict. This is steady-state semantics, not dynamics. With `compare_to`, decide whether the model (a concept, e.g. a triz_transform result) has the baseline's input→deliverable relation; pass segment's or take_out's boxMap as `box_map`. `trim` is shorthand: perform the trim as triz_transform does and compare the result with the model. Verdict preserved; changed (a lost deliverable, or a counterexample input with the differing outputs and which relation contains which); or undecided (reason missing-behavior: the boxes that can reach a deliverable and declare no behaviour; reason no-steady-state: neither model has a steady state at any input, so equal empty relations say nothing). With `joint_boxes` and `weakest_spec`, select every composed box without behavior and compute one coupled residual over their combined ports. The joint rows are a single relation: independentSafe checks whether independently declaring their per-box projections stays inside the target, factorizes checks whether their product equals the joint relation, and a counterexample explains unsafe coupling. The exact search is bounded by max_states; row_costs are unsupported in this mode. With `weakest_spec` (and compare_to or trim), give the weakest box specification (residual in Rel) for the one box of the concept that can reach a deliverable and declares no behaviour, against the same target: spec, every row of that box whose composite stays inside the target, with preserves:true when declaring it gives exactly the target (any behaviour that does is contained in it); impossible, when the spec's composite misses part of the target (an uncovered input is given; no behaviour of that box gives the target, and the empty relation, which always stays inside, is never read as preserving) or a deliverable is lost; undecided for three or more unknown boxes when joint_boxes is omitted (several-holes), missing baseline behaviour, an empty target, or past the cap (state-cap). When the box to specify declares `producible` rows (what it can physically produce), the spec is the residual cut down to them: spec when that still covers the target (producible.infeasible lists the residual rows left out); impossible with reason infeasible when the residual covers the target but its producible rows do not, with requiredInfeasible giving, per missing target pair, the residual rows that deliver it, none producible (every relation that gives the target contains one of each); impossible with reason not-covered when the residual itself does not cover. With exactly two boxes without behaviour (boxes), a pair of relations stays inside the target iff every pair of rows, one of each, does, and the maximal such pairs are the formal concepts of the safe row pairs: spec lists those whose composite covers the target (specs, each declared and re-checked to give exactly the target; every pair that gives the target lies inside one), with weakest:true when there is one and weakest:false when several are incomparable; impossible (not-covered) when none covers, with each maximal pair's uncovered input (pairs); undecided (concept-cap) past the cap on concepts. Producible rows cut each box first; impossible with reason infeasible then means some pair over all rows (wouldGive) would give the target. Fails closed on ill-typed behaviour, an ambiguous or mismatched box_map, inputs whose values differ between the models, and past the state cap. With `certificate: true` and compare_to or trim, supported comparisons return a request-bound Lean equality with nonemptiness or an input/output pair belonging to only one relation; declared box_map, one-sided inputs and gained deliverables follow the comparison's baseline interface and selected scope. With row_costs in the one-hole mode, cheapestExtension gives an exact least-cost set of safe nonproducible rows to add, using the complete target relation and explicit integer costs, or reports an undecided capped search; it is not-applicable (target-not-covered-by-residual) when the residual itself misses the target, and row_costs fail with invalid-row-costs wherever no one-box residual is computed; the Boolean verdict is unchanged. The verdict holds for the relations as declared; substantiating them, the absorber's or mediator's first, is outside the kernel.

BehaviorRow.description: One admissible (inputs, outputs) pair of the box's relation

in.description: Input port id → value; names every input port of the box

out.description: Output port id → value; names every output port of the box

behavior.description: Declared behaviour: a finite relation from input-port values to output-port values over the carriers' declared values. An input tuple with no row cannot occur; several rows for one input tuple are alternatives. Omit when unknown

cost.description: Cost per resource dimension, e.g. { usd_month: 400, latency_ms: 2.5 }; dimensions are never summed together

feasibility.description: Monotone co-design feasibility: the minimal rows the box can work at, each a level provided per output port against the levels it requires per input port and its operating cost. Read monotonically: providing less never needs more, and more resources never hurt. No row may be dominated by another. An output port of an intensive carrier has one level shared by every function on it; on an extensive carrier (`quantity`) the demands of its functions add up. Omit when unknown

initial.description: States the box may start in; a subset of state

inner.description: Nested model and explicit one-to-one outer-to-inner interface bindings

producible.description: For a box whose behaviour is unknown: the rows it can physically produce, over the carriers' declared values, as behavior rows. triz_behavior weakest_spec keeps only these, and reports the rows the target needs that the box cannot produce. A box declares behavior or producible, not both

role.description: Function-analysis role; environment and supersystem boxes are resources outside the engineered system

state.description: Declared state: the finite set of values the box carries from one step to the next. Requires transition

transition.description: Declared dynamics: rows (state, inputs) → (next state, outputs) over the declared state and carrier values, making the box a nondeterministic Mealy machine. A (state, inputs) pair with no row cannot occur; several rows are alternatives. Requires state; a box declares behavior or transition, not both

dimension.description: Unit, protocol, or measure carried, e.g. 'W thermal', 'gRPC request', 'USD/month'

levels.description: Thresholds that read a numeric amount (a feasibility row's level) as one of the declared values (a behavior row's value): an amount reads as the last level whose `from` it reaches. The list orders its values from least to most; the first starts at 0 and each `from` exceeds the one before. Requires values, e.g. [{ value: 'low', from: 0 }, { value: 'high', from: 50 }]

loss.description: Whether the flow is a loss: true when no level of it is wanted from any performer, such as a pressure drop, leakage, noise, or wear; false when some level is. Read only by the defect-on-loss-carrier lint, which then ignores its word list, so the lint gives the same warnings after any renaming. Omitted, the lint guesses from the words of the carrier id, its dimension, and the function verbs. No verdict reads it

quantity.description: How amounts on this carrier combine where one output port feeds several functions. 'intensive' (the default) is one shared level, such as a voltage, a temperature, or a copied message: the port meets the largest demand. 'extensive' is an amount that divides, such as a flow of water or a current: triz_feasibility makes the port supply the sum of the demands, and refuses an extensive input fed by several functions (model a merge box). Declare it explicitly; it is never inferred from the layer

values.description: Finite set of values the carrier can take, e.g. ['low', 'high']; required on every port of a box that declares behavior

from.description: Least amount that reads as this value, in the units of the feasibility rows on this carrier

value.description: A declared value of the carrier

Demand.description: One requirement on the parameter; where a demand omits an axis it applies across that whole axis

values.description: Admissible values of the parameter for this demand

FeasibilityRow.description: One minimal (functionality provided, resources required) pair of the box's monotone feasibility relation

cost.description: Operating resources per cost dimension, added to the box's fixed cost; an omitted dimension needs nothing

provides.description: Output port id → level the box can provide there, in the carrier's dimension; an omitted port provides nothing (level 0)

requires.description: Input port id → level the box needs there to provide this row; an omitted port needs nothing. Only a non-harmful function can supply it

Flow.description: A flow path: the boxes a carrier passes through in series, in order. It records order along the flow, which functions do not: two boxes in series need not act on each other

carrier.description: Carrier id: what moves along the flow, e.g. water, a request, cash

medium.description: The box that stands for what flows, when the boxes on the path act on it rather than pass it on, e.g. a 'water' or 'request' product box

path.description: Box ids in the order the flow passes through them, in series. A box listed again later closes a loop; a box may not follow itself

flows.description: Flow paths: which boxes a carrier passes through, in order. Read by triz_flow and by merge's adjacent reading; the other checks ignore them

provenance.description: Embedded import source locations and explicit analyst review. Draft models cannot drive analysis; review is an assertion, not a proof of source truth

weights.description: Explicit normalization to a scalar ideality: one weight per cost dimension plus 'harmful'

axes.description: Declared cells per axis; defaults to the cells the demands name

TransitionRow.description: One admissible step of a stateful box: in this state, on these inputs, it may move to next and emit these outputs

in.description: Input port id → value; names every input port of the box

next.description: Next state; one of the box's declared state values

out.description: Output port id → value; names every output port of the box

state.description: Current state; one of the box's declared state values

Wire.description: A TRIZ function: a typed wire from an output port of the performing box to an input port of the box acted on

carrier.description: Carrier id; must equal both port carriers

from.description: Output port of the box performing the function

polarity.description: TRIZ function rating: useful at the right level, useful but insufficient, useful but excessive, or harmful

to.description: Input port of the box the function acts on

verb.description: Function verb in base form, e.g. 'heat', 'cache', 'charge'

absorb.description: With trim: function wire id → absorber output port; default: the first absorber triz_trim lists

box_map.description: With compare_to: concept box id → baseline box id, applied to deliverables and boundary inputs; pass a triz_transform segment or take_out boxMap here

certificate.description: With compare_to or trim: independently certify a finite equality or inequality under the selected scope

compare_to.description: Baseline model; with it, decide whether the model preserves the baseline's input→deliverable relation

flows.description: Flow paths: which boxes a carrier passes through, in order. Read by triz_flow and by merge's adjacent reading; the other checks ignore them

provenance.description: Embedded import source locations and explicit analyst review. Draft models cannot drive analysis; review is an assertion, not a proof of source truth

weights.description: Explicit normalization to a scalar ideality: one weight per cost dimension plus 'harmful'

full_relation.description: Return every relation row within the search cap; default output is truncated for display

joint_boxes.description: With weakest_spec: select every composed box without behavior as one coupled joint relation

max_cost_search.description: With row_costs: cap on exact extension-search nodes (default and maximum 100000); a capped search makes no optimality claim

max_states.description: Cap on boundary valuations and search states (default and maximum 100000)

model.description: The model to compose (the concept, when compare_to is given)

flows.description: Flow paths: which boxes a carrier passes through, in order. Read by triz_flow and by merge's adjacent reading; the other checks ignore them

provenance.description: Embedded import source locations and explicit analyst review. Draft models cannot drive analysis; review is an assertion, not a proof of source truth

weights.description: Explicit normalization to a scalar ideality: one weight per cost dimension plus 'harmful'

row_costs.description: With one-hole weakest_spec: explicit cost of every safe nonproducible row that covers an unmet target pair. cheapestExtension finds the least total cost set of additional rows, charging each once. Costs share one caller-chosen unit; no cost is inferred

scope.description: Default upstream assumes omitted boxes accept all received values; whole composes every declared box constraint

trim.description: Boxes to trim; with it, decide whether the trim preserves the external behaviour

weakest_spec.description: With compare_to or trim: give the weakest specification for the one box, or the maximal pairs of relations for the two boxes, that can reach a deliverable and declare no behaviour, against the same target

name: triz_behavior
